sources.entry: Hyper - Terminal built on web technologies.

summary.one_liner: Hyper is a cross-platform terminal emulator built on web technologies and designed to be extended with plugins and themes.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Hyper as a terminal app built on open web standards, with goals centred on speed, stability, and a stable API for extension authors. It is installable via package managers on Linux (AUR, NixOS), macOS (Homebrew Cask), and Windows (Chocolatey), with a note that package-manager versions may lag the latest release. The contributor section covers forking, installing dependencies with pnpm, and running a dev build with watch-and-rebuild plus an Electron launcher. It also explains how to produce distributable binaries with a dist command. Known build issues are documented for node-pty, Xcode, C++ compilation, and macOS code signing. Related repositories are listed for the website, a sample extension, a sample theme, and an awesome-hyper list.
use_cases: build extensions or themes for a terminal
contribute to an Electron-based terminal app
install a terminal on Linux, macOS, or Windows
develop and test a terminal app locally
notable: Built on open web standards, so the UI is web-based
Focus on an extension API for plugins and themes
Installable through AUR, Nix, Homebrew Cask, and Chocolatey
Dev workflow with Webpack watch rebuilds and a VS Code debug launch config
caveats: Package-manager versions (Homebrew, Chocolatey, Snapcraft, AUR) may not be the latest release
Windows development requires windows-build-tools from an elevated prompt
Linux development needs GraphicsMagick, icnsutils or libicns-utils, and xz
macOS builds may need Xcode setup or code-signing workarounds
